title: Semantic Retrieval for Multilingual Technical Documentation
business: Global engineering firms managing technical manuals in multiple languages.
problem: Traditional keyword-based search fails to retrieve relevant technical procedures when terminology varies across languages or synonyms are used, leading to high support costs.
solution: The bge-m3 model provides sentence-similarity capabilities that map diverse queries and documents into a shared vector space, enabling semantic retrieval that transcends exact keyword matching.
steps: Initialize the bge-m3 model using the sentence-transformers library.
Pre-process technical documentation by chunking text into semantically meaningful segments.
Generate dense vector embeddings for all document chunks using the model.
Store embeddings in a vector database to support similarity search.
Transform incoming user queries into the same vector space to retrieve relevant passages.
outcome: Improved retrieval accuracy for cross-lingual technical queries, reducing the time engineers spend searching for correct maintenance procedures.
limitation: The model's performance is sensitive to the length and quality of input chunks; verify effectiveness by monitoring the relevance of top-k retrieved results against known ground-truth queries.

code.content:
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
# Load the bge-m3 model for sentence similarity
model = SentenceTransformer('BAAI/bge-m3')
# Encode documents into vectors
doc_embeddings = model.encode(['Procedure A', 'Procedure B'])
# Encode query into the same space
query_embedding = model.encode('How to fix error X?')
